fields.acceptance: link.txtar checks rhiza link store serves log --json, with --record and with --dry-run, each exits 2 with code usage and the message link type "serves" does not go from capability to capability; a change set serving a capability is refused and a change set serving an intent succeeds; an apply.txtar case with one bad link item refuses the whole apply and adds no entry; a Go table test shows buildLink agrees with check.Allowed for every type and end kinds; existing scripts that wrote bad links are changed to valid ones
fields.statement: rhiza link, apply link items and --record links refuse a link whose type does not go from its from-end's kind to its to-end's kind, by the endpoint table rhiza check uses, as a usage error naming both kinds and writing nothing

fields.acceptance: check.txtar writes a log entry file holding a verifies link from an intent to a capability in an open change set; rhiza check exits 0 and prints warn in-flight change set <id>, op <id>, link <id>: link type "verifies" does not go from intent to capability; a withdrawn change set holding the same link gives no warning
fields.statement: rhiza check warns, rule in-flight, on a link with bad endpoint kinds that is only in a draft, proposed or accepted change set, naming the change set, op and link, so a bad link written by hand or by an older binary shows before it lands
